tasks.title: 'hubble-local-admin' action resets the HugeGraph admin account to admin/admin and writes it to deploy/.env
tasks.description: scripts/container.ps1:254-266 runs scripts.setup_hubble --rotate-local-admin, which sets the graph 'admin' user's password to the literal 'admin' (scripts/setup_hubble.py:20-34), then rewrites HUGEGRAPH_PASSWORD=admin in deploy/.env and recreates the stack. The result is a well-known default credential (CWE-1392/CWE-798) on the graph that holds all ingested data. Mitigations seen: ports bind to 127.0.0.1 (deploy/docker-compose.yml:85), the action is opt-in and prints a warning, and deploy/.env is gitignored. Residual risk: any local process or container on the backend network gets graph admin, and the state persists in volumes after the demo. Priority P2: loopback-only and opt-in, but it persists silently.
acceptance_criteria: Action sets a random password (CSPRNG, ≤48 chars, see FT-X04) instead of 'admin', or requires an explicit --i-understand-demo-credentials flag and refuses when any port binds beyond 127.0.0.1
Hubble UI login uses a separate generated credential that is shown once
A `hubble-local-admin --revert` path (or `up`) restores a random password; docs updated
No literal 'admin' password remains in setup_hubble.py (grep check in CI)
automated_tests: new: unit test: rotate_local_admin never sends user_password == 'admin'
new: container.ps1 lint/pester test: action refuses when EOIP_*_PORT binds 0.0.0.0
